sections.heading: 1. Deforestation and its Effects
points: **Deforestation** = clearing forests and using the land for other purposes.
Causes: farming, industry, buildings, roads, and natural (fires, droughts).
Effects: **less rainfall, floods and droughts, soil erosion, desertification, global warming (more CO₂), loss of wildlife and biodiversity**.

sections.heading: 2. Biodiversity and Conservation Terms
points: **Biodiversity (biological diversity)** = the variety of plants, animals and microbes in an area.
**Flora** = plants of an area; **Fauna** = animals of an area.
**Endemic species** — found **only** in a particular area (e.g. sal, wild mango in Pachmarhi).
**Endangered species** — at risk of extinction; **extinct** = no longer existing.
The **Red Data Book** records **threatened/endangered** species.

sections.heading: 3. Protected Areas
points: **Wildlife Sanctuary** — protects **animals** (some human activity allowed).
**National Park** — protects the **whole ecosystem** (flora, fauna, landscape); no human activity/private rights.
**Biosphere Reserve** — a large protected area to conserve **biodiversity and culture**; may contain sanctuaries and national parks (e.g. **Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve**).
**Project Tiger** (1973) protects tigers; a **Red List (IUCN)** tracks species.

sections.heading: 4. Migration and Reforestation
points: **Migration** — some birds/animals move to distant places seasonally (to escape harsh climate).
**Reforestation** = replanting/regrowing forests on cleared land.
**Afforestation** = planting trees where there were none.
Paper should be **recycled** (saving trees, water and energy).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Deforestation → less rain, soil erosion, floods/droughts, global warming, loss of biodiversity.
Flora = plants, fauna = animals; endemic = found only in one area; Red Data Book = threatened species.
Sanctuary = protects animals; National Park = whole ecosystem; Biosphere Reserve = largest (biodiversity + culture).
Project Tiger (1973); IUCN Red List tracks species.
Reforestation = replant cleared forest; afforestation = plant new forest.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Endemic** = found **only** in one area; **endangered** = at risk of extinction — don't confuse.
**National Park** protects the **whole ecosystem**; a **Sanctuary** protects **animals**; **Biosphere Reserve** is the largest.
The **Red Data Book** lists **threatened/endangered** species.
**Reforestation** = restoring a cleared forest; **afforestation** = new planting.
